verdicts.note: Three independent sources: the website says he has 'opposed every suggestion of a tax increase' [S2], the pamphlet says he has 'refused to take more from your wallet' and backed a tax sunset [S1], and he cast the recorded lone no vote on the 2026 0.1% public safety sales tax [S4]. A vote plus repeated explicit statements supports -2 high. Nothing in the dossier points the other way.

Attacked on strength. The counterweight is his vote to accept the $11.7M Consolidated Homeless Grant [S5], but that is pass-through state money kept under county control, and he questioned it twice on the record ('The more we spend, the more they come') before voting. His stated alternative to the 2026 tax was to reduce county spending [S4]. Two sources on restraint, one ambiguous vote: -2 at medium (not high) is a fair reading.

One-term incumbent elected 2022 [S7], seeking a second term [S6]. KLOG calls him the board's longest-serving commissioner [S6], but four years is still a short tenure, so -1 rather than -2 is consistent with other one- and two-term incumbents in this election.

Attacked on direction. She pairs grant-seeking with stewardship language ('good stewards of our tax dollars' [S1]; 'not about bigger government. It's about smarter government' [S3]), which pulls toward the middle. But her one concrete fiscal position is that the county should compete for outside funding and investment rather than refuse it [S3], which is an invest-and-expand lever and a direct contrast with Dahl's 'more we spend' stance. No new programs are named, so +1 medium, not +2.

No prior office is documented [S1][S2], but she does not run on newness or outsider status. Her pamphlet leads with credentials ('These diverse experiences have allowed me to gain the skills and perspectives necessary to be an effective and creative leader': Peace Corps, county health work, the teen parent program, teaching) and her anti-partisan line ('instead of partisan politics') is about governing style, not renewal [S1][S3]. The opponent is a one-term incumbent, not a long-tenured one. This matches the Clark clerk and other refutations that cut first-time candidates to +1 when they run on credentials rather than on being new. Also, the scorer's basis says she runs 'as a working parent'; nothing in the dossier says she is a parent (S2 mentions only her husband), so that phrase is unsupported and should be dropped from the basis.
